design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 of cni_contract_care (round 2).

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 printed: prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[4, 6, 6, 4]. Assignment: anniversary review (root) 6, contract exit damages 6, fixed-price line correction 4, index line correction 4. Tree = root + 3 prerequisite problems (fan-out); value_input edges 2 (floor 2): both line corrections feed the review's net charges; the exit damages are a state gate.

[Scope snapshot] Task 0 occupies the termination security, the noticed-termination damages and the damages before supply with their three tools. This task claims, disjoint: cni_ext_anniversary_security_review (remit_review_deposit_f4180914, owner=user), cni_ext_contract_exit_damages (bill_contract_exit_damages_2ce88247), cni_ext_passthrough_fixed_price_rebill (credit_fixed_price_line_5b24cf0d), cni_ext_passthrough_index_rebill (credit_index_line_725777e6). Union of both tasks = all seven policies and seven tools.

[Design thesis] Surface goal: 'get that anniversary deposit review settled this month and to pay whatever additional deposit it calls for'. Core value: the review remittance. Hidden chain: the review waits on (a) a rebill credit on every block line of the window billed above the price in force for its cycle, (b) the same for index lines, (c) the damages line of every contract of the business closed in term by a final bill or a switch. All false at frozen_time: the July 2026 cycle was re-rated at 6.62 for the whole cycle although the pass-through notice (2026-06-12) came 19 days before its stated date (new price only from 2026-07-12), and its index line carries a 0.85 adder that an in-term block and index cycle does not carry; the Joliet contract closed by final bill on 2026-08-14 with no damages line. One earlier billing error (the June 2026 capacity line billed on the expired planning-year tag) was already corrected on 2026-07-20 and is not open.

[Why a good test] Without the block-line credit the review computes 714.54, without the index-line credit 738.43, on the opening world 746.71; the computation document alone gives 21248.5; today's grade A gives nothing to pay. The corrections need the owed-notice-period rule (day-weighted July price), the block and index pricing rules, the carrying rate and the repeat-error uplift (one correction on another cycle). The damages need per-day annualization and five rate scales.

[Base-invariant card] cni_billing_correction governs both credits: cni_dispute_lookback (anchor posted_date 2026-08-05, 24 calendar months, same day, inclusive -> ends 2028-08-05; handling 2026-10-13 inside; just-fails 2028-08-06) and cni_one_correction_per_line (no credit names either July line; the only existing credit names the June capacity line). Inherited: 500.00 agent limit (both credits within it), tag revisions and interval corrections are not billing errors (the June correction was a wrong planning-year tag on Beacon Ridge's own line, not a grid-operator revision). Declared overrides in the two correction policies: the credit sentence (carrying credit added), the cycle-level pass-through sentence of cni_market_notices (a cycle straddling the end of the owed notice period is day-weighted), and the block sentence of cni_energy_billing (a partial cycle prorates the block). The index-line policy follows base holdover billing exactly (all kWh; holdover adder unless waived for a missing or non-compliant expiry notice). cni_etf governs the exit damages (status closed; no early_termination_fee line). cni_security_deposit deposit_contract_open (Aurora active) governs the review; cni_agg_deposit_cap ceiling not binding; grade at execution respected.

[Business-object card] Root: Aurora 9c76dfc3-b8cd-487a-85a4-4987c81e02c9. Corrections: block line b09abfd0-3df4-4ff0-b30a-39d57d820130 and index line 60a8a1da-4681-4b25-8bc7-beaef04c296f of the cycle 2026-07-01..2026-07-31. Settled history: June capacity line 0cc229e6-0228-4ce5-b1e3-7272c7233f8b with its credit 23e5c0b2-aabe-47a6-9eaa-3c09a25d596e. Damages: Joliet 9cab0916-de6b-46be-8439-9c8778269a56. The review window counts Aurora supply lines posted 2025-11-04..2026-10-05 (12 cycles by block lines) and every rebill credit posted in the window (the June credit and the two July credits).

[Problem-tree card]
- Edge 1 cni_ext_anniversary_security_review -> cni_ext_passthrough_fixed_price_rebill, value_input, gate adj_win, form state: 'The review amount is fixed only after every block line posted in the review window carries a rebill credit for any part of it billed above the block price in force for its cycle.' ('only after', affirmative; state = a rebill credit standing on each over-billed block line; only the fixed-price line correction posts block-line credits). Derivation: notices (lead 19 days) + July block line at 6.62 for all 31 days + the correction rule -> credit the July block line. Deletion: 714.54 vs 706.25.
- Edge 2 cni_ext_anniversary_security_review -> cni_ext_passthrough_index_rebill, value_input, gate adj_win, form state: 'The review amount is not worked out until every index line posted in the review window carries a rebill credit for any part of it billed above the index price the contract allows.' (negated 'not ... until'; only the index line correction writes it). Deletion: 738.43 vs 706.25.
- Edge 3 cni_ext_anniversary_security_review -> cni_ext_contract_exit_damages, state_gate: 'Before the review amount is worked out, every contract of the same business that closed during its term by a final bill or by another supplier's enrollment must carry its early termination fee line.' ('Before ... must'; only the exit damages policy bills that line). Deletion: the Joliet damages row is missing.
- Order: the three prerequisites commute (each correction's repeat count excludes credits for the pass-through cycle; reverse replay identical: True; review 706.25).

[Factor cards]
Fixed-price line correction (-117.83; baseline_result 0.0): price_in_force_for_cycle (method) day-weighted 6.541935 (baseline new rate -> 0.0); fixed_price_kwh_basis (method) full block-and-index cycle -> block 150000 (baseline metered -> 0.0); fixed_price_carrying_rate 2 months -> 0.03 (-117.1); fixed_price_repeat_uplift one other-cycle credit -> 1.25 (-117.69). Near-miss: the August and September block lines at 6.62 are correct (they begin after 2026-07-12); the June correction is on another cycle.
Index line correction (-457.59; baseline_result 0.0): index_kwh_for_cycle (method) above-block kWh (0.0); index_adder_for_cycle (parameter, multi-source) none in term (0.0); index_carrying_rate (-454.75); index_repeat_uplift (-457.02).
Exit damages (9381.57; baseline_result 10650.27): exit_annual_kwh_basis (method) 11 cycles -> per-day annualization (8173.53); exit_reason_share (multi-source) 0.85 (11037.14); exit_term_left_share 0.90 (10423.96); exit_notice_share 1.10 (8528.7); exit_load_factor_share 0.96 (9772.46); exit_tenure_share 0.95 (9875.33).
Anniversary review (706.25; baseline_result 21248.5): review_months_by_grade grade B -> 1 (13600.0); review_exposure_basis 12 cycles (1920.57); index_price_loading (multi-source) share 0.1252 below 0.15 -> the smaller-share tier 1.05 (92.26); small_business_relief (cross-difficulty bizpower) 12 lines -> 0.06 (1529.25); term_left_scale 0.90 (2138.89); tenure_tolerance 0.05 (1384.87).

[Seed rationale] customer; 3 premises; Aurora contract with 13 calendar-month cycles (block, index above block, capacity, transmission), the June capacity line on the expired tag with its July correction, its deposit, 13 monthly index notices, the short-lead pass-through, capacity and transmission notices; Joliet contract with 11 months plus the final partial cycle, its deposit and the refund after closing; 2 executed quotes; the St. Charles small business agreement with 16 energy and 16 fee lines and the sign-up credit (Illinois: no sales tax). Automatic clauses: no expiry notice due, no holdover, the Joliet deposit refunded once, the review due (anniversary 2026-11-01 within 30 days).

[Persona] Rafael Zamora; volunteers the review request and the Aurora anniversary; credentials on request; Joliet sale and absence of notice only if asked; passive dispute of over-charges and consent to other charges; pays the review amount with the months and grade the agent gives.

[Standard solution] find_customers -> verify -> find_cni_contracts -> find_cni_pricing_requests -> find_premises -> find_cni_notices(Aurora) -> find_cni_billing(Aurora) -> find_cni_deposits -> find_cni_billing(Joliet) -> find_bizpower_agreements -> find_bizpower_billing -> credit the July block line -> credit the July index line -> bill the Joliet exit damages -> hand over -> customer remits the review deposit (1 month, grade B).

[Verification] Round-2 authoring harness (check_compute.build_env/eval_compute with real tool replay): every factor's baseline moves its result; each whole baseline differs from gold; corrections commute; review without each prerequisite as recorded above. Per-task and final gates re-run (difficulty worklog). check_traceability deferred until the KB is published.

[Draft recomputation from visible context] From the rule prose, tool schemas, finder returns and persona: the review rule's three prerequisite sentences lead to the two July lines and the Joliet contract; the correction and damages rules give the three writes; the review on the resulting world gives the remittance. Agrees with gold.

[Revisions] r1 (round 1): pass-through new rate set to 6.62 to keep the block correction under the 500.00 agent limit. r2 (round 1): the 2024 deposit sized on 1500000 kWh so the review requests a positive amount.
r3 (round 2, audit F-3/F-4): the block-line policy became the fixed-price line correction (block lines on block and index contracts, energy lines on fixed structures; new tool credit_fixed_price_line_5b24cf0d replaces credit_block_line_fffec1b8). Its price ladder now has three distinct methods (keep the prior price / day-weight across the end of the owed notice period / take the new rate), each reachable; its kWh ladder prorates a partial block-and-index cycle, uses the block on a full cycle and the metered kWh on a fixed structure (the honest standard for fixed lines). Both deviations from base are declared in its overwrite.
r4 (round 2, audit F-5/F-2): the index-line policy's kWh ladder now bills all metered kWh on real-time index and holdover cycles (base holdover billing), above the block (prorated for partial cycles) on in-term block and index cycles; its adder ladder applies the base holdover waiver (missing or non-compliant expiry notice) — no conflict with base remains.
r5 (round 2, audit F-7): the carrying day-count is no longer a factor; the carrying period is the fixed product convention (whole months x 30 / 360). The fourth factor of each correction is a repeat-error uplift of the carrying rate, read from rebill credits for other cycles in the last twelve months; the world gained the settled June 2026 capacity correction it reads.
r6 (round 2, audit task-1 finding 3): the index price loading tier is now recorded as taken — share 0.1252 below 0.15, smaller-share tier 1.05 — in factor_trace, factor_sensitivity and this dossier.
user_scenario:
You are Rafael Zamora, director of facilities at Vandermeer Cold Storage LLC in Aurora, Illinois, and the company's authorized signatory on its Beacon Ridge Energy accounts. You are friendly and a little chatty, you like to hear where a number comes from, and you never argue about policy. The Aurora warehouse contract at 1900 Bilter Road reaches its second anniversary on November 1, and you understand the security deposit on that contract is looked at again around each anniversary. Your finance team asked you to get that anniversary deposit review settled this month and to pay whatever additional deposit it calls for, today, from the company account. You do not know whether anything is owed or how much; that is what you want the agent to work out, and you will make the payment yourself once the agent sets it up. You do not want anything else on the account changed.

You are calling from your desk line, 6305550193, and you give it so they can pull up the account. When they ask you to verify, you give the last four digits of the company's EIN, 5047, and the mailing ZIP code, 60504; if they need one more detail you add your email on file, rzamora@vandermeercold.com. You do not have the customer number or any contract number handy. If they ask about the company's other sites, the Joliet warehouse at 805 Mound Road was sold in August and the utility closed out that account when the buyer took over on August 14; if they ask whether anyone sent Beacon Ridge written notice before that, you say no, the sale just closed. The company's shop at 412 Industrial Drive in St. Charles buys its electricity from Beacon Ridge on a small-business plan and is staying put.

If the agent tells you that something on the Aurora bills was charged above what the contract allows, you ask them to correct it on the account. If the agent explains that some other charge has to go on the company's account before the review can be settled, you tell them to go ahead and put it on. When the agent gives you the review amount and hands you the payment step, you pay exactly that amount yourself on the Aurora contract, entering the other details the agent tells you to enter, and you read back the receipt number you get. Once the deposit shows as recorded, you thank them and end the call.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The three prerequisites are parallel. The two credits name different source lines; each correction's repeat-error count excludes credits for the pass-through cycle itself, so neither credit changes the other (block credit evaluated after the index credit: -117.83; index credit after the block credit: -457.59); the exit damages read only the Joliet ledger. Replaying the three in reverse order gives a byte-identical terminal state (same_terminal=True) and the same review amount (706.25).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the block-line credit the review computes 714.54 instead of 706.25, and the credit row of -117.83 on line b09abfd0-3df4-4ff0-b30a-39d57d820130 is missing.
Without the index-line credit the review computes 738.43 instead of 706.25, and the credit row of -457.59 on line 60a8a1da-4681-4b25-8bc7-beaef04c296f is missing.
Without the exit damages the Joliet early_termination_fee line of 9381.57 is missing from the terminal state (the review's own figure stays 706.25; state gate).

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario raises only the anniversary deposit review of the Aurora contract. It never names a rebill, the July bill, the June correction, the pass-through, an adder, damages or a termination fee, and never asks whether something must be fixed first. The Joliet sale is stated only if the agent asks about other sites, as a fact matching the records (closed 2026-08-14, no notice). Its prerequisite-related lines are passive: 'If the agent tells you that something on the Aurora bills was charged above what the contract allows, you ask them to correct it' and 'If the agent explains that some other charge has to go on the company's account before the review can be settled, you tell them to go ahead'.
